title: Sales Call Follow-Up and Mutual Action Plan
promptText:
You are a sales professional known for follow-up emails that buyers forward to their colleagues. Using my notes from a [CALL_TYPE] with [PROSPECT], write a follow-up email and a mutual action plan.

My call notes:
[CALL_NOTES]

Our target decision date: [TARGET_DATE]

Please write:
1. A subject line that names the prospect's goal, not our product
2. A short opening that thanks them for one specific thing they shared
3. A recap of what I heard, in their words: their goal, their problems, and what matters most to them, in three to five bullets
4. Anything I promised to send or do, with when I will do it
5. The agreed next steps, each with an owner and a date
6. A mutual action plan as a table (step, owner, target date) running to the decision date, including steps the buyer owns such as security review or budget approval, with any step or date we did not agree marked "to confirm"
7. A one-line close asking them to correct anything I got wrong

Keep the email under 200 words, not counting the table. Only include commitments and dates that are in my notes.
description: This prompt has Gemini turn your notes from a sales call into a follow-up email and a mutual action plan. The email opens by thanking the prospect for something specific, recaps their goal and problems in their own words, lists what you promised and when, and confirms the agreed next steps with owners and dates. The mutual action plan is a table of every step to the decision date, including the buyer's own steps such as security review and budget approval, with anything not yet agreed marked to confirm rather than given an invented date. It suits account executives who want follow-ups that keep deals moving and that buyers can forward internally.

variables.name: PROSPECT
variables.example: Dana, Head of Customer Support, and two of her team leads

variables.name: CALL_NOTES
variables.description: Your notes: their goals and problems, what you promised, and what was agreed
variables.example: Dana's goal: first-response time under 2 hours before the holiday rush (about 6 hours now). Team leads re-route 30 to 40 misfiled tickets a day. Liked the auto-routing demo; asked whether it works with their Shopify order data. I promised the Shopify integration guide and a sandbox login by Friday. Agreed next step: a 45-minute technical call with their IT lead next week, Dana to book it. Budget needs COO sign-off. They will need a security questionnaire completed.

variables.name: TARGET_DATE
variables.description: The decision date you are working toward

tips: Write your notes right after the call, including the prospect's exact phrases. The recap is only as good as the words you captured.
Send the follow-up the same day. The mutual action plan works best while the call is fresh for everyone.
Update the table and resend it after each meeting. It becomes the shared plan for the deal, not a one-off email.
exampleOutput:
**Subject:** Getting first-response time under 2 hours before the holiday rush

Hi Dana,

Thanks for walking us through how your team leads handle misfiled tickets today. It made the problem very concrete.

**What I heard**
- Your goal: first-response time under 2 hours before the holiday rush, down from about 6.
- Team leads re-route 30 to 40 misfiled tickets a day.
- Auto-routing looked promising, provided it works with your Shopify order data.
- Budget sign-off sits with your COO.

**What I'll send:** the Shopify integration guide and a sandbox login, by Friday.

**Next steps**
- Dana: book a 45-minute technical call with your IT lead for next week.
- Me: integration guide and sandbox login by Friday.

| Step | Owner | Target date |
|---|---|---|
| Integration guide and sandbox login | Me | Friday |
| Technical call with IT lead | Dana to book | Next week |
| Security questionnaire | Your IT team, with me | To confirm |
| Budget approval | Your COO | To confirm |
| Decision | Dana and your COO | October 30 |

If I got anything wrong, just reply and I'll fix it.

Best,
[Your name]
